facts.hook: Ancient Rome taxed urine
facts.body: Launderers used urine to clean and whiten clothes. Emperor Vespasian put a tax on collecting it from public latrines.

facts.hook: A Sumerian hymn doubles as a beer recipe
facts.body: The Hymn to Ninkasi, the Sumerian goddess of beer, is almost 4,000 years old and describes the brewing process step by step.

facts.hook: Octopuses have three hearts
facts.body: Two pump blood through the gills and the third sends it round the body. Their blood is blue, too: it carries haemocyanin, a copper-based protein.

facts.hook: Flamingos are pink because of what they eat
facts.body: The colour comes from carotenoids in the algae and tiny crustaceans they feed on. Without them, their feathers gradually fade towards white.

facts.hook: The Mona Lisa has almost no eyebrows or eyelashes
facts.body: A 2007 high-resolution scan suggested Leonardo did paint them and that they faded away with cleanings over the centuries.

facts.hook: There isn't just one «The Scream»
facts.body: Edvard Munch made several versions between 1893 and 1910: two paintings, two pastels and a number of lithographs.

facts.hook: You're born with about 300 bones; adults have 206
facts.body: Many start out as cartilage and fuse as you grow: the skull and the pelvis are each made of several joined pieces.

facts.hook: Your stomach replaces its protective lining every few days
facts.body: The cells lining the stomach are replaced every 3 to 5 days. That keeps the acid that digests your food from digesting the stomach itself.

facts.hook: Carrots weren't always orange
facts.body: The first cultivated carrots were purple and yellow. Orange ones became popular in the Netherlands in the 16th and 17th centuries.

facts.hook: The wasabi in most restaurants isn't wasabi
facts.body: Real wasabi is expensive and hard to grow, so what's usually served is horseradish mixed with mustard and green colouring.

facts.hook: Wild axolotls live only in Xochimilco
facts.body: This amphibian, Axolo's mascot, is native only to the canals of Xochimilco in Mexico City. Since 2021 it has also appeared on Mexico's 50-peso note.

facts.hook: La Paz is the world's highest seat of government
facts.body: Central La Paz, Bolivia, sits about 3,600 metres above sea level. Water boils there at around 87 °C, so cooking pasta takes longer.

facts.hook: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
facts.body: The Great Pyramid of Giza was finished around 2560 BC. Cleopatra died in 30 BC, about 2,500 years later and about 2,000 years before Apollo 11.

facts.hook: Oxford University is older than Tenochtitlan
facts.body: Teaching was already happening at Oxford by 1096. The Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded around 1325, more than two centuries later.

facts.hook: The first computer mouse was made of wood
facts.body: Douglas Engelbart and Bill English built it in 1964: a wooden box with two wheels and a single button.

facts.hook: The microwave oven began with a melted candy bar
facts.body: In 1945 Percy Spencer was working on a radar magnetron when he noticed the sweet in his pocket had melted. The microwave oven followed.

facts.hook: Your brain is 2% of your weight and uses 20% of your energy
facts.body: At rest, the brain burns around a fifth of the body's energy even though it makes up only about 2% of body weight.

facts.hook: Each eye has a blind spot, and your brain fills it in
facts.body: Where the optic nerve leaves the eye there are no light receptors. The brain fills the gap with whatever surrounds it, so you never notice.

facts.hook: You can't see the Great Wall of China from the Moon
facts.body: It's very long but narrow and the same colour as the land around it. Even from low orbit it's hard to make out with the naked eye.

facts.hook: Old cathedral glass doesn't «drip» over the centuries
facts.body: Some old panes are thicker at the bottom because the glass came out uneven and was fitted that way. Glass doesn't flow on a human timescale.

facts.hook: Botanically, bananas are berries and strawberries aren't
facts.body: A berry develops from a single ovary and keeps its seeds inside. Bananas qualify; strawberries carry their seeds outside and are aggregate fruits.

facts.hook: An entire forest in Utah is one living thing
facts.body: Pando is about 47,000 quaking aspen stems growing from a single root system. Genetically it is one individual, among the heaviest on Earth.

facts.hook: Only about a quarter of the seafloor is mapped in detail
facts.body: The Seabed 2030 project aims to map the whole ocean floor at high resolution. So far it has passed only about 25%.

facts.hook: A blue whale's heart weighs about 180 kg
facts.body: It's the largest heart known. One from a blue whale stranded in Canada in 2014 was weighed at about 180 kg, as much as two adults.

facts.hook: Australia is wider than the Moon
facts.body: From east to west, Australia measures about 4,000 km. The Moon's diameter is about 3,475 km.

facts.hook: Canada has the world's longest coastline
facts.body: Counting its thousands of islands, Canada's coastline is over 200,000 km long, enough to circle the Earth almost five times.

facts.hook: The tallest known tree is about 116 metres high
facts.body: It's called Hyperion, a coast redwood in California. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it.

facts.hook: The coldest temperature measured on Earth: −89.2 °C
facts.body: It was recorded at Russia's Vostok Station in Antarctica on 21 July 1983.

facts.hook: The sunlight you see left the Sun 8 minutes ago
facts.body: Light takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to cross the 150 million kilometres between the Sun and the Earth.

facts.hook: A diamond and your pencil lead are the same stuff
facts.body: Both are pure carbon. The difference is how the atoms are arranged: a rigid lattice in diamond, sliding sheets in graphite.

facts.hook: Jurassic Park's T. rex roar is partly a baby elephant
facts.body: Sound designer Gary Rydstrom built it by mixing, among others, a baby elephant, a tiger and an alligator.

facts.hook: Feature films first talked in 1927
facts.body: The Jazz Singer was the first feature film with synchronised dialogue. Its first spoken line: «You ain't heard nothin' yet».

facts.hook: A day on Venus is longer than its year
facts.body: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once on its axis but only 225 to orbit the Sun. It also spins backwards compared with most planets.

facts.hook: Neptune has orbited the Sun only once since we found it
facts.body: A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years. It was discovered in 1846 and only completed its first orbit since then in 2011.

facts.hook: The Olympics used to award medals for art
facts.body: Between 1912 and 1948 there were Olympic medals for painting, sculpture, architecture, literature and music, all on sporting themes.
facts.src: Wikipedia · Art competitions at the Olympic Games

facts.hook: One tennis match lasted 11 hours and 5 minutes
facts.body: John Isner and Nicolas Mahut played it at Wimbledon in 2010 over three days. The fifth set ended 70–68.

facts.hook: Spanish «ojalá» originally meant «if God wills»
facts.body: It comes from Andalusi Arabic law šā llāh. Spanish borrowed thousands of words from Arabic, including almohada (pillow), aceite (oil) and azúcar (sugar).

facts.hook: «Robot» comes from a Czech word for forced labour
facts.body: It first appeared in Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R. The idea of using robota came from his brother Josef.
